topic: AgentsDock: An IDE for Agentic AI Research

key_points: Open-source IDE designed specifically for agentic AI research
Docks Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor in one desktop + mobile workspace
Self-hosted server (git clone AgentsServer + ./install.sh) and desktop/mobile client
Connect multiple servers/devices (lab workstation, home Mac mini, rented GPU box) and switch anytime
View/edit and syntax-highlight code on remote hosts — no separate editor
Full persistent tmux terminal attach from any device
Agents return plots, images, rendered rollouts inline in chat
Optional Tailscale (auto IPs) and tmux support
Clients: macOS 14+, Linux AppImage, Windows 10+, iOS/iPadOS 17+ (TestFlight), Android beta
81 points, 32 comments on HN (ZihuiGeorgia), 3 days ago
Author: opened AgentsDock (ZhengyiLuo) repo Sept 11 2026 (~77 stars) but had worked on it for a while (Releases repo dated July 2026)
visarga: runs 5 agents at once, one 'steering' via tmux + one quality-watch agent; 3 workers on separate tasks
tobyhinloopen: handle state conflicts with worktrees or sandboxes when several agents touch same repo
criticism: 'isn't this just paseo.sh with less features and tightly-coupled tailscale?' (AgentK20)
BrandiATMuhkuh: looks like an 'agent factory' for teams — agents on multiple servers, shared conversations
quietraster: 'an IDE built around agents instead of files is the direction i keep expecting to win'
'The 13 Best Agentic IDEs in 2026' — 4 categories: dedicated agentic IDEs, IDE-embedded, open-source VS Code extensions, CLI tools
Defines truly agentic: AI that plans multi-step task, reads files across codebase, writes code, runs terminal, interprets errors, self-corrects
Cursor (VS Code fork) is dedicated leader; Google Antigravity (multi-agent, 2.0 at I/O 2026) boldest bet; Kiro spec-driven
Autonomy is bar: autocomplete alone isn't agentic
No single best — depends on: parallel agents, local execution, BYOK, plan-approval workflow
2026 shortlist: AIDEN (local multi-agent orchestration), Cursor (best AI editor, background agents), Claude Code (best terminal agent), Devin (best cloud delegation), Cline (best free open-source)
Claude Code/Codex must be installed and paid separately; macOS-only gaps hurt some tools
Two kinds: AI editors that grew an agent (Cursor, Zed, VS Code+Copilot, JetBrains Junie) vs agent workspaces where agent is primary unit
Agent workspace = run many agents in parallel, isolate each task, review results — matches AgentsDock's model
Zed, Cursor 2.0 (up to 8 parallel agents in git worktrees), Devin Desktop; agent-agnostic tools (25+)

stats.fact: AgentsDock open-sourced Sept 11, 2026; ~77 GitHub stars; Releases repo dates to July 2026 (built for months prior)
Launched on Hacker News ~3 days ago reaching 81 points and 32 comments (poster ZihuiGeorgia)
Supports 3 agent backends today: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor
Ships clients on 5 platforms: macOS 14+, Linux AppImage (x86_64/ARM64), Windows 10+, iOS/iPadOS 17+ (TestFlight), Android beta
AgentsDock runs a persistent tmux session per chat attachable from any device and streams inline video/plot outputs (example: loco-mamipulation sim rollout '92.4% success / 0.18m error / 42k steps')
Reference market frame: agentic IDEs split into agent-workspace vs AI-editor-with-agent; Cursor and Google Antigravity anchor the 2026 market, but no leader is purpose-built for research workflows

angles: Positioning gap: Cursor/Codex serve software engineers, but researchers need multi-machine orchestration, remote GPU boxes, and persistent sessions — AgentsDock targets exactly that niche (sim eval / model training / rollout review)
The 'dock for all your agents' concept: run Claude Code + Codex + Cursor side by side, no vendor lock-in
Self-hosted / BYO-agent: privacy for sensitive lab work vs cloud-centric rivals like Cursor or Antigravity
Mobile + tailscale = check on long training runs / experiments from a phone or iPad, not just laptop
Inline artifact review: plots, rendered rollouts, images come back in chat — 'review the run's real output' fits research iteration loop
HN skepticism: only days old, 'resembles paseo.sh', and real questions about repo state conflicts when multiple agents touch one repo (answer: git worktrees/sandboxes)
Emerging 'agent-centric IDE' thesis: an IDE built around agents instead of files (quietraster on HN)
